# Intro

::: callout-tip
### Highlights

| EnrichGT means [enrich]{.underline}ing previously enriched results ($E^2_{\text{enrich}}$) into [g]{.underline}reat [t]{.underline}ables and more ... |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Quick and fast enrichment analysis |
| Simple input format, empowering non-pro users |
| Re-clustering of enriched results provides clear insights |
| User-friendly HTML outputs / Dynamic Documents |
| LLM based result annotation |
| Do a series of things in a single package |
:::

::: {.callout-note}
### Aim and Scope

Please note that the primary goal of `EnrichGT` is to provide researchers in wet labs or clincal doctors, who have been busy all day, with quick and insightful biological interpretations from dry lab data to support their experiments. So all things in `EnrichGT` is **quick and dirty**. Its purpose is to offer a “quick overview”. After this initial overview, you can use more widely recognized tools to generate statistically rigorous results (not necessary though). However, don’t misunderstand—this does not mean that the statistical processes in `EnrichGT` are incorrect. I’ve made effort to ensure their accuracy; they are just less refined. If you need a tool that handles every detail, please use *clusterProfiler* or *Metascape* instead. If you are using `clusterProfiler` to perform validation and do further research, please see [acknowledgment](acknowledgement.qmd) page for citing *clusterProfiler*.
:::

# Install EnrichGT

``` r
install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("ZhimingYe/EnrichGT")
```

The `AnnotationDbi`, `fgsea`, `reactome.db` and `GO.db` were from BioConductor and might be slow to install. If you can't install, please re-check your web connections or update your R and BioConductor, or use [Posit Package Manager](https://packagemanager.posit.co/) to install when using old R.

# Meet EnrichGT

Please see articles on the left! Especially the [basic workflow](basic.qmd) introduction.

::: callout-tip
See [package function page](pkgfuns.html) for further detail params of functions. (For example, how to use a function)

You can use `? function` to get further help when installed.

``` r
?egt_recluster_analysis
```
:::

In most examples of this document, we use a result table of DEG analysis `DEG.csv`. The gene symbols of `DEG.csv` is on the first column without column name. In default `read_csv()` convert the unamed column name to `...1`. So `DEGtable$...1` refers to gene symbols.
